qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

On 20 and 24 October, at least 60 worshippers from the Orthodox Tewahedo Church were killed in attacks in the Oromia region of Ethiopia. In the last four years, a further 458 have been killed in the same region1. These attacks are part of a broader environment of violence and insecurity, in which ancient Christian communities in Africa and the Middle East face threats, displacement and attacks on their religious and cultural presence, particularly in Ethiopia and Eritrea2. The protection of religious freedom is a fundamental European value. However, the systematic threat to Christian communities does not seem to have led to the formulation of a coherent and forward-looking European strategy. The historical and cultural connection between these communities and Europe, but also their importance for stability and pluralism in critical geopolitical areas, make their protection a matter of European interest. The Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy is asked: 1.
Does she recognise that Christian communities in critical geographical areas face severe and recurrent persecution, in some cases threatening their very survival?
How is their protection incorporated into EU foreign policy, especially in relations with countries where such attacks are reported?
Does she intend to develop a coherent European strategy for the protection of threatened Christian communities, with specific diplomatic, humanitarian and political tools?
